title: Map your data, score the risks and handle a breach

say: Map your data, score the risks, and handle a breach.
This is the video for Module 2 of Digital Privacy and Data Protection.
This module turns the law into working tools. It starts with one simple table, the data inventory, also called a data map.

panel.heading: You cannot protect what you have not found
items: A data inventory lists all personal data you hold
Why, where, who can see it, how long it is kept

say: Step one. Start from every place data comes in: paper forms, website forms, WhatsApp numbers, email addresses and apps.

panel.heading: Building your data inventory
items: Start from every form and channel
Follow each data type after it arrives
Walk around and look: cupboards, phones
Ask staff: where else might this be?
Write it down and mark the gaps

say: Step two. Follow each type of data after it arrives. Who copies it, where is it saved, who is it forwarded to?

say: Step five. Write each finding into the sheet and mark anything unnecessary or unprotected.

For example, Bisi did this for her NGO in Ibadan in one afternoon. She found photos of member forms on a staff phone, religion and tribe fields nobody used, and a sheet open to anyone with the link. She fixed all three at no cost.

say: In Google Drive, share with named people, not anyone with the link, and give view only unless editing is needed.

panel.heading: Lock down the tools you already use
items: Drive: share with named people, not the link
Two-step verification on every account
WhatsApp: broadcast lists, not open groups
Phones: screen lock, updates, remote wipe
Paper: locked cupboard, shred old forms

say: Next, compare what the organisation does with each principle, and score every gap. Likelihood of harm from 1 to 5, times impact on people from 1 to 5, gives a score from 1 to 25.

panel.heading: Likelihood times impact

cards.d: Act now. Tunde's clinic: patient sheet with diagnoses open to all 11 staff. 4 times 5 is 20.
Plan a fix. No written retention period for old records. 3 times 3 is 9.
Monitor. An out-of-date privacy notice on the wall. 2 times 2 is 4.

say: 15 or more is high. For example, Tunde assessed a clinic in Abuja where the patient spreadsheet, with diagnoses, was open to all 11 staff. Likelihood 4, impact 5, score 20. Act now.

say: A breach is any incident where personal data is lost, changed, disclosed or accessed without permission. A stolen phone, a list sent to the wrong group, a hacked email. Log it the moment you know.

panel.heading: The first 72 hours of a breach
items: Hour 0: become aware, log it
Hours 0 to 4: contain the damage
Hours 4 to 24: assess the risk
Before hour 72: notify the NDPC if risky
High risk: tell affected people at once

say: Contain the damage first. For example, when Ngozi's shop phone with chats from about 400 customers was stolen, she blocked the SIM, erased the phone remotely and moved WhatsApp to a new phone.

say: Then assess the risk. Her customers' names, addresses and payment screenshots could feed scam calls, so the risk was real.

say: If the risk is high, tell the people affected immediately, in plain language. Ngozi warned customers that the shop will never ask for a PIN or OTP.

panel.rule: The clock starts when you become aware, not when you finish.

say: People can ask for a copy of their data, to correct it, or to delete it. A request needs no special words. Please remove me from your list, sent on WhatsApp, is valid.
Log it, confirm who they are, search every location, act or explain what you cannot do, and reply plainly.

panel.heading: When someone asks about their data
items: Log it the day it arrives
Confirm identity using details on file
Search every place in the inventory
Act, or explain in writing what you cannot do
Reply plainly and close the log

say: To remember. Trace every copy. Delete what you do not need. Score gaps and fix the highest first.
Give each type of data a retention period. And in a breach, contain first, then assess and notify within 72 hours.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Trace every copy: phones, paper, email
Delete stray copies and unneeded fields
Score gaps: likelihood times impact
Each data type needs a retention period
Contain, assess, notify within 72 hours
